title: Does four divide eight thousand five hundred and thirty six?
description: The number is split into its hundreds and its last two digits. The hundreds are whole fours, and thirty six is nine fours, so four divides the number, and Keeko's doubt about the lone digit six is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: split the number after the hundreds place, because the hundreds are whole fours and the last two digits decide. Watch for students who test the last digit alone.

video_script.why: The child splits the number into hundreds and the last two digits, sees that the hundreds are whole fours, and tests the last two digits.
video_script.substitution: Split the number after the hundreds place and test the last two digits for fours.
video_script.wrong_answer: eight thousand five hundred and thirty six is not divisible by four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the number is not divisible by four because its last digit, six, is not a multiple of four. Thirty and six are not multiples of four alone, but together they make thirty six, which is nine fours, and the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, eight thousand five hundred and thirty six is divisible by four

final_answer.spoken: yes, eight thousand five hundred and thirty six is divisible by four, as thirty six is divisible by four

hold_back: Answer: Yes, as 36 is divisible by 4
maths_rules: 100 = 25 x 4, so 8500 = 85 hundreds = 85 x 25 fours = 2125 fours
30 = 7 x 4 + 2 and 6 = 1 x 4 + 2; the two 2s left over make another 4, so 36 = 9 x 4
video_script.design: One idea: split after the hundreds, the hundreds are whole fours, and the last two digits decide. Assumes the count in fours. Wrong idea: the lone last digit decides. The split number stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, eight thousand five hundred and thirty six is divisible by four.
Its last two digits, thirty six, are divisible by four.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks eight thousand five hundred and thirty six is not divisible by four.
The reason is that the last digit, six, is not a multiple of four.
<bookmark mark='join'/>But thirty is not a multiple of four either. Together they make thirty six, which is nine fours.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The last two digits work as a pair, so we read both of them.
